bugs.error_message: Pressing Enter in the login page's email/password fields does nothing
bugs.root_cause: The passkey/magic-link/password login forms (backend/src/main/kotlin/com/adoptu/pages/LoginPage.kt) are plain divs with type="button" buttons, not a <form>, and the frontend only wired click listeners on the buttons - no keydown handling existed anywhere, so Enter had nothing to trigger. Verification was separately confounded for ~40 minutes by Chromium caching /static/js/common.js across every browser_navigate reload: the server sends ETag/Last-Modified but no Cache-Control, so the browser kept executing a stale pre-fix bundle across repeated same-session reloads even though the file on disk was correctly rebuilt each time. Confirmed via window.AdoptuLoginPage.init's live runtime function body differing from the on-disk build, resolved by force-loading the script with a cache-busting query string.
bugs.fix: Added setupEnterKeySubmit(inputId, buttonId) to LoginPageModule (frontend jsMain), wired via keydown listeners on magic-email, password-email, and password-password that call preventDefault() + click() on the corresponding button when e.key=="Enter". Rebuilt via :frontend:jsBrowserProductionWebpack and :backend:processResources, verified live via Playwright with a cache-busted <script src="...?v=timestamp"> reload and a real CDP-level Enter keypress that successfully navigated to /profile.

Registration page always shows "verification email sent, check your inbox" even when no email was actually sent - user requested it several times and received nothing
bugs.root_cause: POST /api/auth/registration-options's re-registration path (existingUser exists but not yet verified) called webAuthnService.resendVerificationEmail(existingUser.id) and discarded its Boolean return value, then unconditionally responded with the localized 'verification email sent' message. resendVerificationEmail() internally checks EmailVerificationService.canSendVerificationEmail() (a 3-emails/day cap enforced via EmailVerificationTokens/EmailVerificationAttempts) and returns false without sending once exhausted - so once a user hit the cap, every subsequent registration attempt silently did nothing while still claiming success. The identical rate-limit condition was already correctly handled on the login-with-password route (checks the boolean, reports 'daily limit' in the error) with an existing passing test - but no one had written the equivalent test for registration-options, so this sibling code path's bug went uncaught.
bugs.fix: Captured the resendVerificationEmail() boolean and branch the response: true -> existing 'verification email sent' message, false -> new 'verification email limit reached' localized message (en/es/fr/pt/zh) mirroring login-with-password's daily-limit wording. Added the missing test 'POST registration-options reports rate limit when daily verification emails exhausted' (mirrors the existing login-with-password test) to AuthRoutesE2ETest.kt. Verified live against a real Postgres-backed dev server: created an unverified user with 3 EmailVerificationAttempts rows already inserted for today, confirmed POST /api/auth/registration-options now returns the honest rate-limit message instead of a false 'sent' claim; confirmed a fresh unverified user with zero attempts still gets the normal 'sent' message (no regression). Full AuthRoutesE2ETest suite passes.

RegisterPage.kt's registerPassword()/registerBoth() never showed error or status messages to the user - message div stayed invisible even though the backend correctly returned an error (e.g. the newly-fixed verification-email rate-limit message)

Since the message element starts display:none (set in init() and again on every form submit), any message set via these two paths - validation errors, 'Registering...'/'Creating passkey and password...' progress text, and API errors - was invisible. User discovered this while testing the just-deployed verification-email rate-limit fix: the backend correctly returned the new honest error message, but nothing appeared on screen.

bugs.error_message: Deployed a 'fixed' production image that still had the old bug - the root Dockerfile's :backend:shadowJar build does NOT regenerate the frontend Kotlin/JS bundle from source; it only packages whatever backend/src/main/resources/static/js/common.js is already committed in git
bugs.root_cause: Committed only the RegisterPage.kt source fix (commit 09a9c3c) without also rebuilding and committing common.js/common.js.map. The Dockerfile's builder stage runs `./gradlew :backend:shadowJar`, which depends on `:backend:processResources` (copies backend/src/main/resources/** as-is) - it never invokes `:frontend:jsBrowserProductionWebpack`, so a docker build from that commit silently packaged the OLD, pre-fix bundle. Built and pushed to ECR, applied via Terraform, and the deployment 'succeeded' with zero errors - only caught by explicitly grepping the deployed bundle's content for the expected fix string instead of trusting a clean build+deploy pipeline run. This is a sharper, deploy-pipeline-specific version of the existing cerebrum lesson 'any edit to frontend/src/jsMain has zero effect until jsBrowserProductionWebpack is run' - it also applies to what gets baked into the production Docker image, not just local dev testing.
bugs.fix: Ran :frontend:jsBrowserProductionWebpack in an isolated clean worktree at the source commit, copied the regenerated common.js/common.js.map into the main checkout, and committed them separately (commit 27fdc01). Rebuilt the Docker image from that corrected commit, extracted app.jar from the built image with `docker cp`+`unzip -p`, and grepped its bundled common.js for the expected fix string BEFORE pushing to ECR this time - this pre-push verification step is now the required practice for any frontend-touching production deploy in this project.

bugs.error_message: The /verify (email verification) page shows "Invalid or expired magic link. Please request a new one." for a broken/expired email-verification token - wrong context, confusing wording
bugs.root_cause: I18n.kt defined the key "invalidOrExpiredToken" TWICE within the same language object literal in every one of the 5 languages: once correctly for EmailVerificationPage.kt's data-i18n="invalidOrExpiredToken" ("The verification link is invalid or has expired."), and again a few lines later with magic-link-specific wording ("Invalid or expired magic link..."). A JS object literal with a duplicate key keeps only the last value, so the magic-link wording silently won for every consumer of the key, including the /verify page which has nothing to do with magic links. Found while testing the login/email-verification flows end-to-end on production per user request.
bugs.fix: Renamed the second (magic-link-specific) definition to invalidOrExpiredMagicLink in all 5 languages, restoring the correct text on /verify. Verified live on production via Playwright: /verify?token=invalid-test-token now shows "The verification link is invalid or has expired."

bugs.error_message: Clicking an invalid, expired, or already-banned-account magic login link silently redirects to a plain /login page with zero feedback - user has no idea why nothing happened
bugs.root_cause: AuthRoutes.kt's GET /api/auth/magic-link-login redirects to /login?error=invalid_token, /login?error=invalid_or_expired, /login?error=not_verified[&resent=true|false], or /login?error=banned depending on outcome, but LoginPageModule.init() never read window.location.search for an error param at all - only showRegistrationNotification() existed, checking solely for registered=true. All 4 error variants were completely silent. Found while testing the login flow end-to-end on production per user request, by directly navigating to each /login?error=... redirect target.
bugs.fix: Added showMagicLinkErrorNotification() to LoginPageModule, parsing the error/resent query params via URLSearchParams and mapping each of the 4 cases to its already-existing i18n message (invalidToken/invalidOrExpiredMagicLink/accountBanned/emailNotVerifiedLogin or verificationEmailResent when resent=true), displayed via the existing register-notification banner with a new red .error CSS variant (matching the app's established red/green .message convention). Verified live on production for all 4 error variants via Playwright.

bugs.error_message: Clicking Save on the profile page never visibly shows "Profile updated!" - the field values just silently reset to the freshly-saved values
bugs.root_cause: saveRoles() called showMessage(msg, "success", I18n.t("profileUpdated")) immediately followed by a synchronous window.location.reload() with no delay - the reload wiped the DOM before the browser ever painted the message, on both the empty-role-changes fast path and the Promise.all(promises) success path. There was also a second, near-duplicate Promise.all(promises...).then block doing the exact same success handling with its own redundant .catch - dead/leftover code from an incomplete refactor. Found while testing the profile flow end-to-end on production per user request; only caught by polling document.getElementById('message') on a tight interval immediately after clicking Save, since a normal page inspection a second later would show nothing (already reloaded).
bugs.fix: Wrapped both window.location.reload() calls in window.setTimeout(..., 1500) so the success message is visible before the page refreshes, and deleted the dead duplicate Promise.all block. Verified live on production by sampling the #message element every 150ms after clicking Save: "Profile updated!" (green .message.success) stays visible continuously from ~150ms to beyond 1350ms, then the page reloads with the saved data.

bugs.error_message: Registration grants a fully authenticated, persistent (7-day) session before the user ever proves ownership of the registration email
bugs.root_cause: Both /api/auth/register (passkey) and /api/auth/register-password called res.setSession(...) unconditionally on successful account creation, with zero isEmailVerified check - unlike every login endpoint (login-with-password, magic-link-login, passkey login), which all correctly call validateVerified() before granting a session. Combined with the 7-day session cookie (Sessions.kt MAX_AGE_SECONDS), anyone could register using an email they don't own and get full, persistent authenticated access - profile edits, password changes, adding a passkey, and (since Rescuer role activation and POST /api/pets have zero verification gate at all, unlike Shelter/Sterilization/Photographer/Temporal-Home which do gate on isEmailVerified before 'activate') creating and publishing pet listings - without ever proving email ownership. Separately discovered while investigating: registerWithPassword/verifyAndRegister insert UserActiveRoles rows directly for every role selected at registration time, entirely bypassing the SAME verification gates that exist on the later 'activate via profile' endpoints for Shelter/Sterilization/Photographer/Temporal-Home - meaning those gates only ever applied to re-activating a role post-registration, not to the initial role selection at sign-up. This second, related gap was reported to the user but not fixed in this pass (flagged as a distinct follow-up).
bugs.fix: Removed res.setSession(...) from both registration endpoints. Simplified RegisterPage.kt's post-registration redirect: all registrations now go to /login?registered=true uniformly (removed needsProfileCompletion()/postRegisterRedirect(), which previously sent role-specific registrants to /profile assuming an active session that no longer exists there). Verified end-to-end both locally and on production: after registering, /profile immediately redirects to /login (confirmed via a genuinely fresh browser context - page.context().clearCookies() - not just document.cookie, since the session cookie is not readable/clearable via JS); logging in with the new, unverified account is still correctly rejected with 'Please verify your email before logging in'. Full AuthRoutesE2ETest registration suite (12 tests) passes unchanged.

bugs.error_message: Registration bypassed the isEmailVerified gate on Shelter/Photographer/Temporal-Home/Sterilization role activation - selecting one of these role checkboxes at sign-up activated the role immediately, with zero verification, even though POST /api/users/{role}-profile (activate=true) already correctly requires isEmailVerified for the exact same activation
bugs.root_cause: registerWithPassword() and verifyAndRegister() inserted UserActiveRoles rows directly for every role selected at registration, going straight to the DB rather than through the gated POST /api/users/{role}-profile activation endpoint. Since a brand-new account is never verified yet at the moment of registration, this meant the 4 role types that DO have a verification gate elsewhere in the codebase had that gate completely skipped for anyone who selected the role at sign-up instead of activating it later from /profile. Follow-up to bug-135 (auto-login-before-verification), found while investigating that issue but fixed as a separate, explicitly-requested follow-up.
bugs.fix: Added ROLES_REQUIRING_VERIFICATION_BEFORE_ACTIVATION = {PHOTOGRAPHER, TEMPORAL_HOME, SHELTER, STERILIZATION_SERVICE} and excluded it from the role set inserted at registration in both endpoints. Selecting one of these roles at sign-up now just records intent on the form; activation only happens via the already-gated /profile endpoint after the user verifies + logs in. Adopter/Rescuer/Admin are unaffected (they have no verification gate anywhere in the system - a separate, still-open issue). Added a regression test (POST register-password does not activate roles that require email verification) directly querying UserActiveRoles after registering with all 6 roles selected, confirming the 4 gated roles are absent while Adopter/Rescuer are present. Full registration suite (13 tests) passes. Deployed and confirmed the registration flow completes correctly on production; direct DB-level confirmation relies on the passing local E2E test since production DB credentials are appropriately access-gated from this session.

bugs.error_message: Rescuer role activation and pet publishing had zero email-verification gate anywhere, unlike Shelter/Sterilization/Photographer/Temporal-Home which all correctly require isEmailVerified before activation
bugs.root_cause: Rescuer was the one role type never given a verification gate at all (not a bypass of an existing control like the other 4 - it simply never had one). POST /api/users/rescuer-profile (activate=true) had no isEmailVerified check, registration inserted RESCUER into UserActiveRoles unconditionally, and POST /api/pets only checked activeRoles.contains('RESCUER'), never verification status. Combined, an unverified account (or one whose email will never be verified, e.g. impersonating someone else's address per bug-135) could become a Rescuer and publish pet listings immediately. Explicit user follow-up request after fixing bug-135/bug-137.
bugs.fix: Added the same isEmailVerified check to POST /api/users/rescuer-profile (activate=true) that Shelter/Sterilization/Photographer/Temporal-Home already have. Added RESCUER to WebAuthnService's ROLES_REQUIRING_VERIFICATION_BEFORE_ACTIVATION so registration can't bypass it either. Additionally added a direct isEmailVerified check inside POST /api/pets itself (not just at activation time) as defense-in-depth for this flagship content-creation action, admin-exempt like the existing role check on the same endpoint. Marked the shared PetsRoutesE2ETest rescuer fixture (user id 1, used across 30+ tests) as verified since those tests assume a normal legitimate rescuer. Updated the prior registration test's RESCUER assertion from true to false. Added 3 new regression tests: rescuer-profile activation 403 for unverified user, pet creation 403 for unverified rescuer. Full AuthRoutesE2ETest/UsersRoutesE2ETest/PetsRoutesE2ETest suites pass. Deployed; live-verified the registration flow (with Rescuer selected) still completes normally end-to-end - direct reproduction of the old exploit is no longer possible via the UI at all now, since there's no way to reach an authenticated-but-unverified state after bug-135's fix, which is itself confirmation the gap is closed.

bugs.error_message: Session cookie (user_session) Set-Cookie header had HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax but no Secure flag, found during a final end-of-session security review of the whole auth flow
bugs.root_cause: setSession()/clearSession() never appended `; Secure` to the Set-Cookie header, so the auth cookie was technically eligible to be sent over plain HTTP. HSTS (max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains) and CloudFront mitigate this in practice, but neither protects a client's very first-ever request to the domain.
bugs.fix: Added `; Secure` to both Set-Cookie strings in setSession() and clearSession(). Applied unconditionally (no dev/prod gating) per user instruction. Verified byte-for-byte in the built artifact via `strings` on SessionsKt.class extracted from the shadowJar before pushing (both cookie strings contain 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax'). Full AuthRoutesE2ETest/UsersRoutesE2ETest/PetsRoutesE2ETest suites pass unchanged. Deployed to production (task-definition adoptu:19, image digest sha256:b3648c128442a34b144b186a60e8f8e56bbe1f7fc0eb577429be4dae55c73444); ECS rollout reached COMPLETED steady state and the old task drained cleanly.

bugs.error_message: Client-side photo compression silently falls back to uploading the original, uncompressed file - no visible error, uploads still succeed
bugs.root_cause: img-src CSP directive had no blob: entry. ImageCompression.kt loads the selected file into an via URL.createObjectURL(file) before drawing to canvas; the browser blocks that load under strict CSP, img.onerror fires, and the code falls back to resolving with the original file. Pre-existing since the client-side compression feature was first built earlier in the same session - never caught because uploads still 'succeeded', just uncompressed.
bugs.fix: Added blob: to the img-src CSP directive in SecurityHeadersFilter.kt.

bugs.error_message: POST /api/pets/{id}/images returns 500 in production: "Certificate for <adoptu-pets.adoptu-dynamic-images.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com> doesn't match any of the subject alternative names"
bugs.root_cause: Two compounding pre-existing bugs, unrelated to the WebP/JPEG work: (1) application.conf's storage.prod block had 'bucket = ${?ADOPTU_S3_BUCKET}' followed by a hardcoded 'bucket = "adoptu-pets"' - in HOCON, later assignments win, so the hardcoded literal (a bucket that doesn't exist in the AWS account) always overrode whatever Terraform set via the env var, regardless of its value. Same inverted-precedence bug also affected region/path_style_access, harmlessly since those happened to match. (2) infra/ecs.tf set ADOPTU_S3_ENDPOINT to aws_s3_bucket.dynamic_images.bucket_regional_domain_name (an already bucket-specific virtual-hosted-style hostname); combined with S3ImageStorageAdapter's pathStyleAccess=false, the AWS SDK prepended the bucket name onto that endpoint AGAIN, producing an invalid doubled hostname that fails TLS SNI/cert validation. Found while running the requested S3 image upload verification test against the live production deploy - blocked ALL photo uploads (PNG included), not just WebP, and predates this session's changes entirely.
bugs.fix: application.conf: swapped the override order so the hardcoded default comes first and the env var substitution comes second (matching the correct pattern already used for db.prod.url). infra/ecs.tf: removed the ADOPTU_S3_ENDPOINT env var entirely for prod - the AWS SDK resolves the correct virtual-hosted-style endpoint on its own with no override needed; an endpoint override is only required for LocalStack in dev.

bugs.error_message: Registration-time role selections for RESCUER/PHOTOGRAPHER/TEMPORAL_HOME/SHELTER/STERILIZATION_SERVICE were silently dropped instead of being granted after email verification

But the excluded roles were never persisted anywhere - registerWithPassword/verifyAndRegister just discarded them, so there was no mechanism to grant them later. A user who checked 'Rescuer' at signup saw only ADOPTER after verifying their email, and had to rediscover and re-select the role manually on /profile.
bugs.fix: Added a PendingRoleActivations table (userId, role composite PK) to persist the deferred role selections at registration time (both registerWithPassword and verifyAndRegister). Added UserRepositoryPort.addPendingRoleActivations/consumePendingRoleActivations. UserService now takes a PhotographerRepositoryPort dependency and calls a new activatePendingRoles(userId) helper from verifyToken()/verifyTokenAndGetLanguage() right after email verification succeeds, consuming the pending set and dispatching each role to its existing activate*Profile method (photographer via the injected repository, the rest via UserRepositoryPort). Auto-grant on verification, per user's explicit choice of the 3 presented fix options.

bugs.error_message: Pet photo uploaded successfully (200) but the image doesn't render on the pet detail page - src returns 403 Forbidden

This bug was previously masked by bug-181 (the broken ADOPTU_S3_ENDPOINT that made uploads fail entirely before ever reaching getImageUrl); fixing bug-181 exposed this separate, previously-latent bug. Also fixed extractKeyFromUrl() (used by deleteImage) to parse the key from the URL's path component via java.net.URI instead of a bucket-name substring match, so it works correctly for both the new CDN URL format (bucket not in the path) and the existing LocalStack path-style format (bucket in the path, stripped when pathStyleAccess=true).

bugs.error_message: Passkey LOGIN (navigator.credentials.get() flow) would fail webauthn4j signature verification in production for every real user
bugs.root_cause: WebAuthnModule.authenticate()'s success handler only extracts and sends credential.id, credential.rawId, and credential.response.clientDataJSON to POST /api/auth/authenticate. It never reads credential.response.authenticatorData or credential.response.signature, both of which are always present on a real AuthenticatorAssertionResponse per the WebAuthn spec and are required by WebAuthnService.verifyAndAuthenticate()'s webAuthnManager.verify() call (real ECDSA signature check against the stored public key). Confirmed by hand-building a genuine WebAuthn registration+authentication ceremony from Python (matching WebAuthnServiceTest.kt's WebAuthnCeremony test helper) while seeding demo data - registration succeeded, but there was no way to reconstruct a login request that would pass verification without those two fields, because the real browser client-side code that would normally supply them doesn't. Never caught because backend tests build authentication responses directly in Kotlin (WebAuthnCeremony.buildAuthenticationResponseJson does include authenticatorData+signature) rather than going through the actual frontend serialization code, so the gap only exists in WebAuthn.kt, not in the server or its test suite.
bugs.fix: Fixed frontend/src/jsMain/kotlin/com/adoptu/frontend/WebAuthn.kt's authenticate() success handler: now base64url-encodes credential.response.authenticatorData and credential.response.signature (and credential.response.userHandle when present) into the JSON body sent to POST /api/auth/authenticate, matching the exact field names webauthn4j's AuthenticatorAssertionResponse expects (@JsonProperty "clientDataJSON"/"authenticatorData"/"signature"/"userHandle", confirmed by reading the library's source jar). Reused the existing arrayBufferToBase64() helper instead of duplicating the manual byte-loop. Compiles clean (:frontend:compileDevelopmentExecutableKotlinJs); needs a real end-to-end browser passkey login test before/after deploy since it can't be verified via curl.

bugs.error_message: The ENTIRE passkey subsystem was broken in production: POST /api/auth/registration-options (unauthenticated, the real 'Register with a Passkey' button), POST /api/auth/registration-options-for-user (authenticated add-a-passkey), and GET /api/auth/assertion-options (login) all failed or silently returned an empty/wrong body
bugs.root_cause: Root-caused via CloudWatch Logs (/ecs/adoptu log group, AWS_PROFILE=adoptu): kotlin.reflect.jvm.internal.KotlinReflectionInternalError: Unresolved class: class com.adoptu.services.auth.WebAuthnService$RegistrationOptionsResponse. RelyingParty/PublicKeyUser/PubKeyCredParam/RegistrationOptionsResponse/PublicKeyOptions/AssertionOptionsResponse were all declared as nested `data class`es INSIDE the WebAuthnService class body. jackson-module-kotlin's kotlin-reflect-based introspection (used to find each class's primary constructor for serialization) cannot resolve a nested class's Kotlin @Metadata under GraalVM native-image's closed-world reflection model - this is a known kotlin-reflect limitation for nested/local classes, distinct from a plain missing-reflect-config-entry problem. It silently manifested two different ways depending on where in Jackson's serializer-lookup path the failure was caught: registration-options and registration-options-for-user threw all the way out to an unhandled 500, while assertion-options apparently hit a different fallback path and returned 200 with an empty `{}` body instead of the real challenge/rpId/userVerification fields. Confirmed empirically against production before the fix: POST /api/auth/registration-options -> 500, POST /api/auth/registration-options-for-user -> 500, GET /api/auth/assertion-options -> 200 {}.
bugs.fix: Moved all six DTOs out of WebAuthnService's class body to top-level classes in the same file (WebAuthnService.kt), matching how every other successfully-serialized DTO in the codebase is declared. Left AuthenticatedUser/AuthResult/RegistrationResult nested since they're never passed directly to res.send() (only used internally, then mapped to separate top-level DTOs) and never exhibited the bug. Updated the one test file referencing the old WebAuthnService.X qualified names (WebAuthnServiceChallengeStoreTest.kt, same package so a plain unqualified reference works). Also added the missing GraalVM reflection entries for all 6 relocated classes to backend/src/main/resources/META-INF/native-image/com.adoptu/adoptu-backend/reachability-metadata.json (allDeclaredConstructors/Methods/Fields, matching the existing pattern for every other DTO) - top-level alone fixes the kotlin-reflect resolution error, but production still needs the standard reflect-config entry to let native-image's closed-world analysis find these constructors at all, same as every other DTO in this file. Full :backend:test suite (1309+ tests) and :frontend:compileDevelopmentExecutableKotlinJs both pass. NOT YET DEPLOYED - needs a native-image build -> Docker -> ECR push -> tofu plan/apply cycle before this is live.

bugs.root_cause: activatePhotographerProfile (PhotographerRepository.kt) inserts a Photographers row with country=null/state=null by design (it's meant to be filled in later via PUT /api/users/photographer-settings) - my seed script only called the role-activation endpoint (POST /api/users/photographer-profile {activate:true}) and never the settings endpoint, so GET /api/photographers?country=Mexico's WHERE country=? filter excluded the null-country rows. bugs.error_message: Intermittent, hard-to-diagnose login/passkey failures under real ECS horizontal scaling: password login sometimes fails as invalid-credentials even with the right password, and WebAuthn registration/assertion sometimes fails as invalid-credential, both correlated with which ECS task handled which request.
bugs.root_cause: CryptoService was a singleton object that generated a fresh in-memory RSA-2048 keypair per JVM startup, never persisted. The frontend fetches the public key from GET /api/auth/encryption-key (whichever ECS task answers), encrypts the password client-side with it, then POSTs to a login/register endpoint that may land on a DIFFERENT task with a DIFFERENT keypair - CryptoService.decrypt() silently returns null on the mismatch, which every call site treats as "invalid credentials" rather than surfacing the real cause. Separately, WebAuthnService.ChallengeStore held WebAuthn registration/assertion challenges in a plain in-memory mutableMapOf (plus a single global var for the assertion challenge) - a challenge created on one task was invisible to a different task handling the signed completion request, and the map was unbounded (only ever removed on retrieval, never expired), so a flood of registration-options requests could grow it without bound until a restart.
bugs.fix: Persisted both to Postgres, following the existing DB-backed pattern (see LoginAttempts for rate limiting). Added CryptoKeys (singleton row, id=1) and WebAuthnChallenges (keyed rows with expiresAt) tables in Models.kt, registered in DatabaseFactory.listOfTables. CryptoService.initialize() now loads the persisted keypair on first use (or generates+persists one, with a synchronized+insert-then-fallback-select race guard for concurrent first callers) instead of minting an ephemeral one; added an internal resetForTesting() hook to simulate a fresh ECS task/JVM in tests. WebAuthnService.ChallengeStore was rewritten to read/write WebAuthnChallenges directly (no in-memory map at all) with a 5-minute TTL and opportunistic cleanup of expired rows on every store, keeping the exact same store/retrieve/remove call sites so no caller changes were needed. Added TestDatabase.initH2() wiring (H2 in Postgres-compat mode, same pattern used by every other DB-backed unit test) to CryptoServiceTest and WebAuthnServiceChallengeStoreTest/WebAuthnServiceTest which previously ran with zero DB dependency, plus new tests: CryptoServiceTest verifies the same public key round-trips after simulating a JVM restart via resetForTesting(); WebAuthnServiceTest verifies a challenge is actually a row in webauthn_challenges (not process memory) and is consumed on use, and that a second, independently-constructed WebAuthnService instance can complete a ceremony started by another instance. Updated DatabaseFactoryTest (table count 25->27, added the two new tables to the ordered list) and DatabaseFactoryInitIT to cover the new tables.

bugs.error_message: AuthRoutesE2ETest: register-password role assertions (e.g. 'adds ADMIN role for admin email') fail with 'Expected value to be true' -- UserActiveRoles is always empty after self-registration.
bugs.root_cause: applyRoleSelection(userId, effectiveRoles) computes `immediate` (roles that do NOT require email verification, e.g. ADOPTER/ADMIN) vs `pending` (roles that do), but then calls userRepository.addPendingRoleActivations(userId, ...) for BOTH buckets -- it never inserts the immediate roles into UserActiveRoles directly. The retired native WebAuthnService.registerWithPassword/verifyAndRegister inserted immediate roles into UserActiveRoles directly (UserActiveRoles.insert{...}) and only routed verification-gated roles through pending activation. Additionally the migrated /api/auth/verify-email handler never calls anything equivalent to the old UserService.activatePendingRoles()/consumePendingRoleActivations() after verifying, so even the verification-gated roles never get activated post-verification either. Net effect: no self-registered role (via /register-password or the passkey /register path) ever reaches UserActiveRoles anymore.
bugs.fix: FIXED. Added UserRepositoryPort.addActiveRoles(userId, roles) (UserRepository.kt) mirroring the dedupe-check pattern of addPendingRoleActivations. AuthRoutes.kt's applyRoleSelection now calls addActiveRoles(...) for the immediate bucket instead of addPendingRoleActivations(...) for both. UserService.activatePendingRoles (previously private, used only by the retired native verifyToken()/verifyTokenAndGetLanguage()) is now internal and called directly from /api/auth/verify-email after a successful AuthKit-gated verification, so verification-gated roles activate too. Re-enabled the 4 disabled tests + the activeRoles assertion in 'GET me' -- all pass.

bugs.error_message: AuthRoutesE2ETest: 'POST resend-verification fails for already verified user via form email' / '...for authenticated already-verified user' fail with 'Expected value to be false' -- resend-verification reports success for an already-verified user.
bugs.root_cause: The migrated resend-verification handler (both the unauthenticated form-email branch and the authenticated branch) calls resendActivationEmail(...)/EmailVerificationService.generateAndSendActivationEmail(...) unconditionally, with no isUserVerified(...) guard beforehand. The retired native WebAuthnService.resendVerificationEmailByEmail/resendVerificationEmailDetailed explicitly checked isUserVerified first and short-circuited to failure -- that guard was dropped during the AuthKit migration.
bugs.fix: FIXED. Added an isUserVerified(userId) guard at the top of both branches (form-email and authenticated) in /api/auth/resend-verification, returning VerificationResponse(success=false, ...) immediately for an already-verified user, restoring the retired native WebAuthnService.resendVerificationEmailByEmail/resendVerificationEmailDetailed behavior. Re-enabled the 2 disabled tests -- both pass.

bugs.error_message: AuthRoutesE2ETest: 'GET assertion-options returns challenge' (and every test that calls it, e.g. real-passkey 'authenticate' tests) fails with 500 -- io.helidon...Unhandled exception / InvalidEmailException.
bugs.root_cause: The handler always calls startPasskeyLogin.start(StartPasskeyLoginUseCase.Command(email = "")) -- it never reads a username/email from the request, hardcoding "" to mean a 'usernameless' ceremony start. But AuthKit's WebAuthnCredentialRepositoryAdapter.getCredentialIdsForUsername(username) wraps that string in the domain Email value class (com.universaliun.auth.backend.domain.model.user.Email), which validates a regex and throws InvalidEmailException for "". RelyingParty.startAssertion(...) calls that lookup whenever a non-null username is supplied to StartAssertionOptions, so this throws on EVERY call to this endpoint, uncaught -> 500. The retired native implementation used a dedicated no-arg webAuthnService.generateAssertionOptions() that never needed a per-user lookup. This is a full, user-facing break of the entire 'log in with passkey' start step in production, not just a test artifact.
bugs.fix: FIXED at the library level (per project convention: fix libs in the libs). AuthKit's StartPasskeyLoginUseCase.Command.email is now nullable (default null) -- StartPasskeyLoginService only calls StartAssertionOptions.builder().username(...) when email is non-null/non-blank, producing a real usernameless/discoverable ceremony instead of wrapping "" in the Email value class and throwing. PasskeyLoginStartRequest.email (AuthKit's own mounted-route DTO) made nullable too. Adopt-u's GET /api/auth/assertion-options now passes email = null. Also had to fix two follow-on issues surfaced by real end-to-end ceremony testing: (1) TestHttp.loginAs/loginAndGetCookie only captured the FIRST of multiple Set-Cookie headers via firstValue(), silently dropping the AuthKit access-token cookie set alongside the native session cookie -- fixed to join all Set-Cookie headers. (2) a usernameless assertion response MUST carry response.userHandle (Yubico has no other way to identify the account) -- the test's simulated-authenticator helpers didn't set it; threaded the real AuthUserId (Adopt-u's int user id, UTF-8 encoded per AuthKit's WebAuthnCredentialRepositoryAdapter convention) through as userHandle. Re-enabled all 4 disabled tests -- all pass. Published AuthKit with this fix (also added `cause` chaining to PasskeyLoginFailedException/PasskeyRegistrationFailedException while debugging, a real diagnostic improvement for any consumer).

bugs.error_message: AuthRoutesE2ETest: 'POST register succeeds with a real ceremony but reports failure when the verification email cannot be sent' fails with 'Expected value to be false' -- setFailMode(true) on the mock notification adapter has no effect on the response.
bugs.root_cause: Neither the passkey /api/auth/register handler nor the password /api/auth/register-password handler ever actually dispatches a verification email. AuthKit's FinishPasskeySignupService.finish/RegisterService.register both return `activationToken`/`email` in their Result specifically so the HOST builds the activation link and sends it -- the exact 'library never emails, host builds the link and sends' contract AuthRoutes.kt already honors correctly for forgot-password and request-magic-link. But both /register handlers ignore result.activationToken entirely and just reply success=true/emailVerificationSent=true whenever result.requiresEmailVerification is true (a config-derived flag, not an actual send outcome).
bugs.fix: FIXED. Added a sendActivationEmail(activationToken, email, user) helper in AuthRoutes.kt that builds the verification URL from AuthKit's own already-persisted result.activationToken (same 'library never emails, host builds link and sends' contract already used for forgot-password/request-magic-link) and sends it via NotificationPort using EmailVerificationService's existing localized templates (getLocalizedContent, already internal). Both /api/auth/register and /api/auth/register-password now call it and report the real send outcome instead of a config-derived flag. Re-enabled the 1 disabled test -- passes.

bugs.error_message: After rewriting TestServer.kt's registerTestLogin() to mint an AuthKit JWT cookie (for AuthRoutesE2ETest), the full backend test suite went from 0 failures outside auth E2E tests to 256 failures across PetsRoutesE2ETest/UsersRoutesE2ETest/PhotographerRoutesE2ETest/etc. (401s and 'No session cookie returned from test login' errors).
bugs.root_cause: registerTestLogin() is shared test infrastructure used by many E2E suites beyond AuthRoutesE2ETest. Route groups other than AuthRoutes.kt (Pets/Users/Photographer/Shelter/TemporalHome/Sterilization/...) have NOT been migrated onto AuthKit yet and still authenticate via the native req.getSession() cookie. The first version of the fix set ONLY the new AuthKit access-token cookie and stopped setting the native SessionUser session cookie, breaking test-login for every still-native route group; it also threw when the test userId had no AuthKit-visible row (some tests deliberately log in as a nonexistent id to exercise a downstream 404), which surfaced as 'No session cookie returned from test login' since the 500 response carried no Set-Cookie header at all.
bugs.fix: registerTestLogin() now sets BOTH cookies unconditionally: the native SessionUser session cookie first (unconditional, exactly as before -- keeps every not-yet-migrated route group's test-login working), then best-effort mints and sets the AuthKit access-token cookie only when the userId actually resolves via UserRepositoryPort.findById(...) (skipped, not thrown, for deliberately-nonexistent test userIds). Full suite re-run confirmed clean after this fix.

bugs.error_message: AuthRoutesE2ETest 'register-password adds ADMIN role for admin email' failed: role list was [ADOPTER], missing ADMIN, even though the test's own AppConfig set admin.email=admin@test.com matching the registered email.
bugs.root_cause: TestServer.start()'s effectiveModules composed the caller's own `modules` list first, then appended a config fallback module (`module { single { config } }`) LAST -- using TestServer's own internal config (admin.email=admin@adopt-u.com from defaultTestConfig()), not the caller's. Koin silently lets the last-registered definition for a type win on a collision (no error), so this fallback silently overrode any test's own AppConfig binding, including admin.email overrides -- the actual adminEmail value used by AuthRoutes.kt's registration handlers was always the default, never the test's override.
bugs.fix: Reordered effectiveModules so the config fallback and authKoinModule come FIRST, and the caller-supplied `modules` (or default appModule(config)) come LAST -- so a caller's own AppConfig binding wins, as originally intended by the fallback's own doc comment ("append a fallback ... so it's always resolvable", never meant to be authoritative). Verified the full backend suite (1323 tests) still green after the reorder.

bugs.error_message: Session cookies used SameSite=Lax; user policy requires Strict
bugs.root_cause: AuthKit CookieConfig defaulted to SameSite=Lax and adoptu hardcoded Lax on access/refresh/legacy session cookies; Lax was unnecessary since no flow reads cookies on a cross-site request (OAuth state is server-side, magic links auth via URL token)
bugs.fix: Changed all cookie sites to SameSite=Strict; magic-link-login now returns a same-origin meta-refresh bounce page instead of 302 so the first /profile render carries the Strict cookies; updated AuthRoutesE2ETest + AuthKit CookieAuthRoutesTest; published AuthKit backend snapshot

bugs.error_message: e2e-verify Playwright suite: 26 failures — 'Invalid credentials' for all seeded users (admin@adoptu.com etc.)
bugs.root_cause: test_data.sql password hashes predate the AuthKit cutover: argon2id with m=65536,t=3,p=4 and a 64-byte digest. AuthKit's PasswordHasher.verify() compares against a fixed 32-byte digest, so those hashes can NEVER verify regardless of password. Additionally the hash wasn't even of Test1234!.
bugs.fix: Regenerated the shared seed hash in AuthKit's exact format (argon2id m=16384,t=2,p=1, 16-byte salt, 32-byte digest) for Test1234!, updated test_data.sql and live user_passwords rows. Also cascade-deleted 65 half-registered leftover e2e users (created by two accidentally-concurrent Playwright runs) via FK-metadata-driven deletes.

bugs.error_message: Server-rendered pages and legacy routes (UIRoutes /admin, Photographer/Shelter/SterilizationLocation routes) treat every logged-in user as anonymous — /admin redirects to /login, nav never shows logged-in state
bugs.root_cause: AuthKit cutover regression: those consumers authenticate via the legacy user_session HMAC cookie (web/Sessions.kt getSession), but after the cutover no login path set that cookie anymore — only adoptu_access/refresh_token
bugs.fix: setAuthCookies now also takes a SessionUser and re-issues the legacy user_session cookie at all three login sites (password, passkey, magic link)

bugs.error_message: AuthRoutesE2ETest: 9 tests suddenly 401 after adding setSession to login responses
bugs.root_cause: Helidon ServerResponse.header(SET_COOKIE, ...) REPLACES the Set-Cookie header, silently dropping the access/refresh cookies previously added via headers().addCookie() on the same response
bugs.fix: setSession/clearSession converted to headers().addCookie()/clearCookie() so all cookies coexist

bugs.error_message: Browser e2e registration fails: 'password must have at least 2 uppercase letters, must not contain your name'
bugs.root_cause: Suite password Test1234! predates AuthKit PasswordPolicy (>=10 chars, >=2 upper, >=2 lower, >=1 special, no name/email fragment — 'test' collides with the seeded @test.com addresses)
bugs.fix: Global test PASSWORD changed to SuperClave99!!; seed hash regenerated in AuthKit format; docs updated in test_data.sql header + AGENTS.md

bugs.error_message: Password registration rejects valid passwords ('must not contain your name') and, pre-policy, stored hashes of the wrong string — password-registered users could never log in
bugs.root_cause: RegisterPage encrypts "email:password" as one RSA payload (same as login), but register-password passed the decrypted COMBINED string into AuthKit RegisterUseCase without the substringAfter(':') unwrap login does — so PasswordPolicy validated 'email:password' (name/email fragments always match) and the stored hash was of 'email:password'
bugs.fix: Unwrap with substringAfter(':', decrypted) before RegisterUseCase.Command, mirroring login-with-password

bugs.error_message: Changing or setting a password via /api/users/password locks the account out of password login
bugs.root_cause: PasswordService hashed with password4j Argon2Function(65536,3,4,64,ID,19) — a 64-byte digest. AuthKit PasswordHasher.verify() compares a fixed 32-byte digest, so login could never verify these. Same generator produced the unverifiable pre-cutover seed hashes

bugs.error_message: Logout leaves all auth cookies alive in the browser (nav still shows logged-in; access/refresh cookies survive)
bugs.root_cause: Helidon ServerResponseHeaders.clearCookie(name) emits the expiry Set-Cookie WITHOUT a Path attribute; the browser scopes it to the request directory (/api/auth), which never matches cookies stored with Path=/
bugs.fix: clearAuthCookies/clearSession now emit explicit SetCookie with path("/") and Max-Age=0 for all four cookies

bugs.error_message: Every emailed verification link lands on 'Verification Failed — invalid or expired' (server-rendered /verify page)
bugs.root_cause: AuthKit cutover gap: registration stores the activation token as sha256 on Users.resetTokenHash, and /api/auth/verify-email was updated to check that slot — but the /verify PAGE route (the one the email actually links to) still validated only the old EmailVerificationTokens table
bugs.fix: /verify now checks the resetTokenHash slot first (activate + clear token + activatePendingRoles + legacy user_session login), keeping the old-table path as fallback for pre-cutover links; UIRoutesE2ETest Koin module gained AdoptuUserRepositoryAdapter
